To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The projected climate change in the eastern Mediterranean is characterized by reduced frequency of the regional wet systems and shorter wet systems duration, (2) the reduction in the frequency of the regional synoptic systems is projected to be the main factor affecting rainfall amount and streamflow volumes and (3) the projected reduction in the streamflow volumes is larger than the projected reduction in annual rainfall.

the projected climate change will lead to a substantial reduction in rainfall and streamflow amounts, and a shortening of the streamflow season, with a greater reduction in streamflow volumes than in rainfall amounts, due to the reduction in soil moisture.
the projected reduction of rainfall in the study catchments is mainly due to the reduction in the occurrence frequency and the duration of wet synoptic events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of regional meteorological synoptics systems changes on rainfall and stream flow patterns, and their implications for the hydrological regime.
the impact of regional synoptic climate change on the hydrology of catchments in convective rainfall environments.
the hydrological sensitivity of catchments in a convective environment to climate change, using high spatiotemporally resolved rainfall scenarios.

the hydrological regime in the study area is projected to be significantly affected by climate change.
the reduction in rainfall amounts is projected to be larger than the reduction in streamflow volumes.
the hydrological response of the catchments is highly dependent on the rainfall patterns and the hydrological response to rainfall is more amplified than the projected rainfall reduction.

the projected reduction in the number of rainfall events, the reduction in their duration, and the reduction in soil moisture are the dominant factors in the reduction of the streamflow volumes in the catchments, and that these reductions are amplified relative to the reduction in rainfall amounts.
